# Multiple Instance Learning

A learning setup where labels are attached to bags of instances rather than to each instance. In pathology the bag is a slide, the instances are its tiles, and the label is a slide-level diagnosis or biomarker.

## How It Is Used

Tile embeddings from a [[foundation-model]] are pooled into one slide representation, often with attention weights that indicate which tiles drove the prediction. Slide-level models such as [[xu-2024-prov-gigapath-whole-slide-foundation-model]] replace simple pooling with long-context transformers.

## Why The Distinction Matters For Us

The [[colorectal-metastasis-atlas]] needs spatial maps, not slide labels. Attention weights look like maps but are not calibrated estimates of cell-type abundance. [[amara-okonkwo]] made this point when someone suggested using attention heatmaps as a proxy for deconvolution; the [[pathology-foundation-model-evaluation-sketch]] therefore uses tile embeddings regressed on Visium HD-derived cell-type fractions instead.
